name: atomic_issue
fields: cycles: per-SM atomic unit admission interval of one warp-wide atomic instruction, linear in atomic_same_address_lanes (max number of active lanes of the instruction that target the same address)
purpose: The engine serializes ATOM / ATOMG / ATOMS / RED / REDG / REDS instructions per SM on TIME kind 15 (start = max(now, frontier), frontier = start + cycles). h100 carries a predecessor table re-expressed over same-address lanes (8.5 .. 37.1, experimental, no probe in the repo) and b300 carries 0 (placeholder). One new probe measures the quantity on both devices.
probe: new tools/microbench/atomic_issue/probe/atomic.cu: one CTA, W warps (W = 1 on SMSP 0; W = 4, one per SMSP), each warp: bar.sync; t_s = clock64; U independent atomics with no use of any returned value; t_e = clock64; bar.sync. Ops (SASS form checked): red.global.add.u32 (REDG / RED.E.ADD), atom.global.add.u32 with the result written to a register that is never read before t_e (ATOMG.E.ADD), atom.shared.add.u32 (ATOMS.ADD), red.shared.add.u32 (ATOMS / REDS form as compiled), generic atom.add.u32 on a global pointer (ATOM.E.ADD). Lane addresses: lanes grouped in blocks of L consecutive lanes; block b targets base + b x 128 B (global: one L2-resident line per block, warmed before the window; shared: distinct banks), so atomic_same_address_lanes = L, L in {1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32}. U in {8, 16, 32, 64} straight-line. --launches 8 --reps 33, two runs; SASS gate: exactly U atomic instructions of the expected opcode in the window and no other memory instruction.

derivation.slope(op, L, W): OLS slope over U of the per-U median of (t_e - t_s)
derivation.cycles(op, L): slope(op, L, W = 4) / 4  (four SMSPs feeding one per-SM unit: the per-SM admission interval)
derivation.diagnostic: slope(op, L, W = 1) is reported; if slope(W = 1) >= 0.9 x slope(W = 4) the bound is per SMSP, not per SM, and the result is recorded as an open engine question (kind 15 scope); the install still uses the W = 4 definition

acceptance.cell: fit max relative residual <= 5 % and run agreement <= 5 % -> measured, else experimental and listed
acceptance.h100_control: the installed h100 table is not a protocol value; it is replaced, the old points are kept in the source description

install: <arch>/leaves/storage.atomic.issue.json: per operation_class, cycles linear(atomic_same_address_lanes) knots at L in {1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32}; ATOM (generic) from the ATOM.E cell, ATOMG / RED / REDG from their global cells, ATOMS / REDS from the shared cells. Source keys atomic_issue.<device>.<run>. One two-architecture 450 A/B round.
not_allowed: no case-cycle tuning; no values from other machines; no threshold or derivation change after data

addenda.before_run: h100-r2 / b300-r2 (written after full-gpu-chain-report.md 8.6 found the installed ATOMG 61.6 cycles/SM makes one stream-K fixup hop cost 512 x 61.6 = 31.5 k cycles while the whole hardware kernel takes 77 k (<= 4 k per hop, <= 8 cycles per ATOMG); before any probe change was built or launched)
addenda.text: (1) Gap: the r1 probe's U straight-line atomics of one rep all reuse the same per-lane address, so within one warp instruction i+1 hits exactly the lines instruction i is still updating: the window measures the per-line read-modify-write follow-on interval at L2 under four warps (same-line chain), not the per-SM admission interval of independent atomics that the leaf storage.atomic.issue.cycles is defined as and that the engine applies to every atomic of an SM (TIME kind 15). r1 evidence that it is a shared-resource effect rather than a fixed per-SM interval: slope(W=1)/slope(W=4) = 0.15 (atomg) / 0.26 (redg) on both devices, i.e. the per-warp time per instruction grows 4-7x when three more warps run on disjoint lines; all r1 cells were experimental (OLS max relative residual far above 5 %: the U = 8 point is absorbed by the in-flight queue). (2) Probe (atomic.cu, template parameter IND = 1): same CTA / warps / bar.sync / clock window / lane blocks of L same-address lanes as r1, but instruction i of the U targets base + warp x 512 KiB + i x 4 KiB + b x 128 B, so no two instructions of a rep touch the same line and the lanes-per-line axis L is unchanged; the 2 MiB (4 warps x 512 KiB) is read once into L2 before the window; U in {16, 32, 64, 128} (U = 8 dropped: inside the in-flight queue in r1; 128 is the largest U whose returned values fit the register file of one warp); W in {1, 4}; ops redg / atomg / atom only (shared atomics have no L2 line and their r1 cells stand); --launches 8 --reps 33; two runs per device in one job; the r1 same-address variants are run again in the same job as the control. SASS gate as r1 (exactly U atomics of the expected opcode in the window, no other memory instruction; the per-instruction offsets are immediates). (3) Derivation: cycles_indep(op, L) = (med(U=128) - med(U=64)) / 64 / 4 at W = 4 (steady-state per-SM admission interval; the U = 16 / 32 points only locate the in-flight-queue knee); steady = |inc(64->128) - inc(32->64)| / inc(64->128); diagnostics reported, not gated: W = 1 increment ratio (as r1), 4-point OLS max relative residual. (4) Acceptance per cell: run agreement of inc(64->128) <= 5 % and steady <= 10 % (both runs) -> measured; else experimental and listed, not installed. Control (per device, both runs): the same-job same-address atomg and redg L = 1 W = 4 r1-style slope / 4 must reproduce the installed r1 values (h100 61.63 / 31.61, b300 54.50 / 34.13) within 10 %; a failed control means the device or run is suspect and nothing from that device is installed. (5) Install: storage.atomic.issue.cycles ATOMG <- atomg.indep, ATOM <- atom.indep, RED / REDG <- redg.indep, linear over the L knots as r1, only cells with verdict measured on a device whose control passed; ATOMS / REDS keep r1. Source keys atomic_issue.<device>.r2; the r1 same-address figures stay in the source description as the per-line follow-on interval. If an installed cell differs from its r1 value by more than 20 % an open item is recorded: consecutive same-line atomics within one SM serialize at L2 and kind 15 carries no per-line state (candidate axis atomic_line_reuse, not introduced by this addendum). One two-architecture A/B round (full GPU 500 x 2 and single cluster 500 x 2) after install. (6) not_allowed as the body: no case-cycle tuning, no values from other machines, no threshold or derivation change after data.

addenda.before_run: h100-r3 / b300-r3 (written after the r2 analysis — atomic_issue.<device>.r2 sources — and after reading the stream-K fixup ATOMG addresses from $A/fg-speed/gsr-diag/cutlass_stream_k_splitk_06/out-cpp/job.bin: 32 lanes x 4 B = one 128 B line (4 sectors) per instruction, consecutive instructions 512 B apart; before any probe change was built or launched)
addenda.cells: atomic.{redg,atomg,atom}.L1.W{1,4}.S{4,8,16,32,64} (lines sweep) and atomic.{redg,atomg,atom}.L{2,4,8,16,32}.W{1,4}.S4 (same-word sweep inside one line); the r2 .indep cell is the S = 128 point
addenda.text: (1) Gap: r2 showed the per-SM interval of a warp-wide global atomic is not reduced by giving every instruction fresh lines (h100 atomg 74 vs r1 61.6, redg 32 = r1; b300 58 / 32), so the cost is not same-line reuse; both r1 and r2 put the 32 lanes on 32 distinct 128 B lines at L = 1 (block stride 128 B), while the coalesced pattern of real kernels (stream-K fixup, atomicAdd epilogues: 32 lanes x 4 B in one line) was never measured. The leaf axis atomic_same_address_lanes cannot see the difference (both are L = 1). (2) Probe (atomic.cu, kernel argument sbytes = block stride): as r2 (IND = 1, instruction i at base + warp x 512 KiB + i x 4 KiB, U in {16, 32, 64, 128}, W in {1, 4}, 2 MiB warmed into L2, --launches 8 --reps 33, two runs per device in one job) but block b of L same-address lanes targets + b x S bytes: lines sweep L = 1, S in {4, 8, 16, 32, 64} -> distinct lines per instruction S / 4 in {1, 2, 4, 8, 16} (sectors S in {4, 8, 16, 32, 64}); the r2 .indep cell (S = 128) is the 32-lines point and is re-run in the same job; same-word sweep S = 4, L in {2, 4, 8, 16, 32} -> one line, 32 / L distinct words. Ops redg / atomg / atom. SASS gate as r1 / r2 (exactly U atomics of the expected opcode, no other memory instruction). (3) Derivation per cell: r2 rule — cycles = (med(U=128) - med(U=64)) / 64 / 4 at W = 4, steady = |inc(64->128) - inc(32->64)| / inc(64->128); W = 1 ratio and 4-point OLS residual reported. (4) Acceptance: per cell run agreement <= 5 % and steady <= 10 % (both runs) -> measured, else experimental and listed; controls per device: the r1-style same-address atomg / redg L = 1 W = 4 slope / 4 within 10 % of r1 AND the re-run S = 128 L = 1 cell within 10 % of the r2 value for redg (both devices) and for atomg / atom where r2 was measured (b300); a failed control voids the device. (5) Install: the leaf storage.atomic.issue.cycles of the GLOBAL classes changes axis to cache_line_count (distinct 128 B lines touched by the instruction; the converters' existing capture axis function, declared in common/axes.json as kind int / owner capture / unit count): linear with knots cache_line_count in {1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32} = the L = 1 cells S in {4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128}; ATOMG <- atomg, ATOM <- atom, RED / REDG <- redg; a class is installed on a device only if all six knots are measured and the device's controls hold, otherwise that class keeps its current leaf and the gap is listed. ATOMS / REDS keep atomic_same_address_lanes (shared memory has no cache line; the mechanism's field_models declaration becomes linear over axes_subset_of [atomic_same_address_lanes, cache_line_count]). Same-word sweep: if at S = 4 the cycles over L in {1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32} spread by more than 10 % of the L = 1 value, an open item records the second dependence with the numbers (the leaf stays single-axis; no 2-D model is invented); the engine's TIME kind 15 is unchanged. Source keys atomic_issue.<device>.r3. The r1 / r2 figures stay in their source descriptions. One two-architecture A/B round (full GPU 500 x 2 and single cluster 500 x 2) after install. (6) not_allowed as the body: no case-cycle tuning, no values from other machines, no threshold or derivation change after data.

addenda.before_run: h100-r4 / b300-r4 (written after the r3 analysis — atomic_issue.<device>.r3 sources; RED / REDG installed on cache_line_count, ATOMG / ATOM not installed because their W = 4 sweeps are not steady over U; before any probe change was built or launched)
addenda.text: (1) Gap: for returning atomics (atomg, atom) the r3 W = 4 one-line medians over U = 16 / 32 / 64 / 128 are 111 / 412 / 843 / 2340 (h100): the window measures issue back-pressure, U = 16 x 4 warps still fits in flight, and the 64 -> 128 increment is 1.7x the 32 -> 64 one (steady 0.4; b300 0.11-0.22 at 1 and 16 lines), so no ATOMG / ATOM cell met the r2 / r3 gate although the one-line value (5.8 / 4.9 cycles) is the quantity stream-K needs. Reading (inference): the per-warp return path saturates near 64 outstanding ATOMG, so a 4-warp sweep to U = 128 mixes two bounds. (2) Probe: same kernel (IND = 1, block stride S), launched with W = 16 warps (512 threads, four per SMSP; __launch_bounds__(512) for U <= 64, the U = 128 kernels keep 128 threads so their returned values stay in registers) and U in {16, 32, 64}: 16 x 16 = 256 atomics in flight from the first point, the per-SM path is saturated throughout and no warp holds more than 64 returned values; out[] / sink / gbuf (16 x 512 KiB = 8 MiB, L2-warmed) sized for 16 warps; W = 1 / 4 cells unchanged and re-run as controls; two runs per device in one job; --launches 8 --reps 33. SASS gate as before. (3) Derivation per W = 16 cell: cycles = (med(U=64) - med(U=32)) / 32 / 16; steady = |inc(32->64) - inc(16->32)| / inc(32->64). (4) Acceptance: per cell run agreement <= 5 % and steady <= 10 % -> measured, else experimental and listed; controls per device: the r1 same-address atomg / redg L = 1 W = 4 cell within 10 % of r1, and the W = 16 redg lines knots (1 .. 32 lines) within 10 % of the r3 REDG install (h100 5.0 / 10.0 / 20.0 / 40.0 / 48.0 / 32.0, b300 5.08 / 8.07 / 16.06 / 31.99 / 31.99 / 31.99) — W = 16 must measure the same per-SM quantity as W = 4 where W = 4 was steady; a failed control voids the device. (5) Install: ATOMG <- atomg, ATOM <- atom on cache_line_count (knots 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 lines = S 4 .. 128 at L = 1) when all six knots are measured and the controls hold; RED / REDG keep r3 (the W = 16 redg cells are the control, not a new install); same-word sweep at W = 16 reported, open item as r3 if the spread exceeds 10 %. Source keys atomic_issue.<device>.r4. One two-architecture A/B round after install. (6) not_allowed as the body.

addenda.before_run: h100-r5 / b300-r5 (written after the r4 analysis — no ATOMG / ATOM cell met the r2-r4 steady gate on h100 although the W = 4 and W = 16 one-line values agree within 25 % across runs and devices; the user authorised a gate definition suited to returning atomics; no probe change; a fresh run is judged, the r4 data is not re-judged)
addenda.cells: the r4 W = 16 cells (atomic.{redg,atomg,atom}.L1.W16.S{4,8,16,32,64}, .W16.indep, .L{2..32}.W16.S4; U in {16, 32, 64}); W = 1 / 4 cells re-run as controls
addenda.text: (1) Gap: the window of this probe measures issue back-pressure; for returning atomics the U sweep is concave (the in-flight queue absorbs the first ~16-24 instructions per warp, and beyond ~64 outstanding per warp the return path adds a second bound), so no increment-based gate (r2-r4: adjacent increments within 10 %) is met even when the value is reproducible (r4 h100 one-line atomg 4.61 both runs, b300 4.63; r3 W = 4 5.8 / 4.9). With W = 16 the per-SM path is saturated from U = 16 on and T(U) / U is flat from U = 32 (r4 h100 atomg one-line 73.7 / 73.7 cycles per warp-instruction at U = 32 / 64; U = 16 is 56.6, still in the fill). (2) Derivation per W = 16 cell: cycles = mean over U in {32, 64} of T(U) / U / 16 (T = per-U median of the window; the saturated per-SM interval); flat = |T(64)/64 - T(32)/32| / mean. (3) Acceptance: flat <= 10 % and run agreement of cycles <= 5 % -> measured, else experimental and listed; controls per device: r1 same-address atomg / redg L = 1 W = 4 cell within 10 % of r1, and the W = 16 redg lines knots (this derivation) within 10 % of the r3 REDG install; a failed control voids the device. (4) Install: ATOMG <- atomg, ATOM <- atom on cache_line_count (knots 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 lines) when all six knots are measured and the controls hold; RED / REDG keep r3; same-word sweep reported, open item as r3 if the spread exceeds 10 %. Source keys atomic_issue.<device>.r5. One two-architecture A/B round after install. (5) not_allowed as the body.
